# Joey in Sync

> Joey (Nikolaj Krištof Jochym) is a community architect and author. He launches, repairs and staffs online communities, mostly on Discord: onboarding, governance, staff teams, events, growth and outreach, and the writing that holds it together. Seven years founding, running and directing communities. Open for work.

Every figure on this site comes from server message logs, member counts and dated announcement records. Case studies state what was measured and what was not.

## What clients hire Joey for

- Launch a community: server architecture and roles, launch plan and opening events, onboarding and first-contact flow, rules, moderation and security, initial staff structure.
- Fix a dying community: community audit and diagnosis, retention and channel restructure, feedback and reactivation loops, events and engagement systems, growth and partnership plan.
- Build a team that runs it: staff roles and departments, recruitment and application flows, training and operating standards, escalation and accountability, clean handoff and continuity.
- Growth and outreach: community research and lead sourcing, partnership development, Discord partnership outreach, creator and community collaborations, outreach tracking.

## Case studies

- [Guildstew](https://joeyinsync.com/guildstew.html): a Discord built for a Kickstarter community. Onboarding, backer access, support, feedback and staff operations in one server, handed over with practical documentation. Client project, delivered October 2026.
- [Project Aurora](https://joeyinsync.com/aurora.html): a cold launch driven from 9 messages on day one to 2,508 on day fourteen, and the onboarding, governance, canon and security systems built to hold it.
- [Crimson Network](https://joeyinsync.com/crimson.html): an international multi-game community that peaked at ~1,400 members, and the staff structure built to outlive its founder.
- [Site-202 "New World"](https://joeyinsync.com/site202.html): a six-day teaser campaign before a single feature shipped, 4,000+ messages on launch day, 100 members in a week, and a founder account compromise the community never felt.

## Reference

"Joey built the backbone of both my communities. On Aurora he took an empty server to thousands of messages a day and designed the onboarding, rules and events that kept it running. On Crimson he built and trained a staff team that ran itself after he moved on. He's who I'd trust with community structure." — Mikey, Owner & Founder, Crimson Network / Project Aurora
